trajectory.description: Completed her undergraduate degree in physics at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel.

trajectory.title: PhD from Vrije Universiteit Brussel
trajectory.description: Completed her PhD in physics, having already published early work on wavelet theory and time-frequency analysis.

trajectory.title: Joined AT&T Bell Labs
trajectory.description: Moved to AT&T Bell Laboratories as a researcher, working at the intersection of mathematics and signal processing.

trajectory.title: Constructed compactly supported wavelets
trajectory.description: Published her groundbreaking construction of compactly supported wavelets, now known as Daubechies wavelets, revolutionizing signal processing.

trajectory.title: Professor at Princeton University
trajectory.description: Appointed professor of mathematics at Princeton University, becoming the first tenured woman in the mathematics department.

trajectory.title: President of the International Mathematical Union
trajectory.description: Served as president of the IMU from 2010 to 2014, the first woman to hold the position.

trajectory.title: Joined Duke University
trajectory.description: Moved to Duke University as professor of mathematics and electrical and computer engineering.

trajectory.title: Continued research at Duke
trajectory.description: Remains active at Duke University, continuing work on applied mathematics and wavelet theory.
